name: Bell Semiconductor
old_description: Bell Semiconductor is the successor in interest to the intellectual property portfolio that originated at Bell Labs following the invention of the transistor.  Semiconductor-related R&D continued as Bell Labs became part of Lucent Technologies, and then subsequently continues as a core competency of successor companies: Agere Systems, LSI, Avago and Broadcom.
about:
Bell Semiconductor is based in Chicago, Illinois. The company traces its lineage to the intellectual property portfolio that originated at Bell Labs following the invention of the transistor. That portfolio passed through Lucent Technologies, Agere Systems, LSI, Avago, and Broadcom before becoming the foundation of Bell Semiconductor. Key leaders include Chad Hilyard and Sailesh Merchant, both of whom previously held leadership roles in the intellectual property businesses at Lucent, Agere Systems, and LSI.

Bell Semiconductor licenses a semiconductor intellectual property portfolio that covers technologies enabling continued integration of semiconductor devices. The portfolio is licensed to virtually all foundries and integrated device manufacturers, supporting production of smartphones, PCs, tablets, wearables, and IoT devices. The company does not manufacture physical products; its business centers on patent licensing and technology transfer.

Its customers span the semiconductor manufacturing industry, including foundries and integrated device manufacturers that produce chips for consumer electronics, mobile communications, and internet-of-things markets. Licensees include major players in the smartphone, PC, tablet, wearable, and IoT device sectors.

The company exists to maintain and monetize the historic Bell Labs transistor patent portfolio, ensuring that foundational semiconductor inventions remain available to the industry. Its leadership’s deep experience in IP management at Lucent, Agere, and LSI positions it to administer this portfolio across the global semiconductor supply chain.
